intro: If you're after a budget stay in Bangkok that's the "easiest to get around from" — Cloudy Hostel is a name backpackers bring up a lot in the Phaya Thai area · This is a small hostel on Soi Pathumwan Resort, Phaya Thai Rd, Ratchathewi, set off the main road and into a soi, which keeps it quieter than you'd expect, yet still under a 5-min walk to BTS Phaya Thai and the Airport Rail Link — these two lines take you to Siam, Asok, Chatuchak and run straight to Suvarnabhumi Airport without ever sitting in traffic · What real reviews mention most is clean rooms, comfy beds, large secure lockers, and friendly staff who are happy to suggest places to go · There are dorm beds and private rooms, from about THB 350–900/night, scored around 9.2 from real reviews on Trip.com

body.html: Who Cloudy Hostel is for — to put it as simply as possible, Cloudy Hostel is a hostel for "travelers who put easy transport and budget first" in Bangkok · It's not a party hostel with a bar blasting all night, and it's not a fancy boutique hostel selling design · It's a small, simple 2-star place sitting on Soi Pathumwan Resort on Phaya Thai Rd, Ratchathewi, a spot where "getting anywhere next is easy" because it's close to both the BTS and the Airport Rail Link · Real reviews line up on this: the people who fit here are backpackers, solo travelers, budget couples, and small families booking a private room rather than anyone chasing luxury or full-hotel amenities · Another group that says they were impressed is people who land late or fly out early, because the Airport Rail Link is just a short walk away, making it easy to haul a bag in and out of Suvarnabhumi Airport without paying for a pricey taxi · The place is still open today and keeps scoring well, with around 9.2 on the main booking platform, and TripAdvisor lists it among Bangkok's positively reviewed specialty lodging · You could call it a hostel that plays the "good value and convenient" angle to the full, while still keeping up the cleanliness standards that budget travelers care about most

Location and getting around — this is Cloudy Hostel's number-one selling point, no question · The hostel sits on Soi Pathumwan Resort, just off Phaya Thai Rd, in Thanon Phaya Thai subdistrict, Ratchathewi district · What makes this location special is that it's only about 250 meters — under a 5-min walk — from both BTS Phaya Thai and the Airport Rail Link Phaya Thai station · The BTS Sukhumvit Line takes you to Siam, Chit Lom, Asok, Thong Lo and up to Chatuchak–Mo Chit in a few stops, while the Airport Rail Link runs straight to Suvarnabhumi Airport in about 30 min without any traffic · That's why international travelers love this location so much, because they barely need a taxi at all · Beyond the trains, you can also walk to Pratunam Market and Bangkok's big clothing-shopping district within about 1 kilometer, and CentralWorld and Siam Paragon are just a few BTS stops away · Victory Monument, where you catch vans to other provinces, is close by too · One small note is that Phaya Thai Rd is a busy main road, but because the hostel is set back into the soi, several reviews say "step just a little away from the chaos of the main road and it gets a lot quieter" — a nice balance between easy travel and being able to rest

"Great location, just a few minutes' walk from BTS Phaya Thai, plus you can connect to the Airport Link straight to the airport · The hostel is set back into the soi a bit so it's quieter than expected, big lockers, clean bathrooms, and free coffee and cookies too — really good value at this price"

Room types and decor — Cloudy Hostel has around 14 rooms in total, covering several types so you can pick by budget and group size · For the most budget-minded travelers there are beds in a shared dorm and a female-only dorm for women traveling solo, which many reviews praise for making them feel safer · For more privacy there are several private rooms: a Double Room with a big bed for couples, a Twin Room with a private bathroom for two friends, a Triple Room with a balcony at around 32 sqm that's roomier than a typical hostel room, and a Quadruple Room with bunk beds for groups or families · The decor is simple and clean, leaning bright, not luxurious but looking new and tidy · Every room has air conditioning, which matters a lot in Bangkok's heat · Many reviews agree that the rooms are very clean, the beds more comfortable than expected, and the bathrooms clean · Something travelers bring up often is the large secure lockers that fit a whole backpack or a big suitcase, which is hard to find in a hostel at this price and lets solo travelers relax about their belongings · Some private rooms have an en-suite bathroom, while dorm beds use shared bathrooms that reviews say are clean with good hot-water pressure

Amenities and common area — as a 2-star hostel, Cloudy Hostel doesn't have a pool or a hotel-style gym, but it has the essentials covered for a budget stay · The common area has lounge sofas, a TV, a fridge, and a microwave to share, handy for anyone buying food from a convenience store or the market outside to heat up · Something many reviews especially like is the free tea, coffee, and cookie corner that's refilled all day, a small touch that makes you feel looked after · There's luggage storage before check-in or after check-out, which is really useful for late flights, laundry for travelers staying several days, and free Wi-Fi throughout the building that reviews say works well · The large secure lockers outside the dorm room also count as an amenity backpackers care about · To be straight with you, the place has no elevator — it's a walk-up building, a point that comes up in reviews, especially for anyone with a big suitcase or several bags · Overall the vibe leans clean, tidy, and quiet rather than flashy, which matches the guests who stay here well

Food and eats nearby — Cloudy Hostel doesn't serve breakfast or have its own restaurant, which is normal for a hostel in this price range, but on location it has a big advantage, because the Phaya Thai–Ratchathewi area is full of restaurants and street food at friendly prices · Walk a few minutes out of the soi and you'll find rice-and-curry shops, noodle stalls, made-to-order spots, and cafes spread all along Phaya Thai Rd · Around BTS Phaya Thai and the Victory Monument side are popular street-food spots open late, good for anyone coming back after a full day out · There's a 24-hour convenience store within walking distance, so you can grab a snack or drinking water anytime · For anyone who wants to cook or heat up food, the common area has a fridge and a microwave · And the free tea, coffee, and cookies in the lobby help cover a light breakfast · Put simply, food isn't something you need to rely on the hostel for, because the moment you step out the door there are plenty of options at prices cheaper than eating in a hotel — one of the charms of staying in this area

Service — service is another point that gets steady praise in real reviews · Cloudy Hostel's staff are often described as friendly, smiling, and ready to recommend places to go, restaurants, and how to get around for travelers visiting Bangkok for the first time · Many people say they got good tips on taking the BTS, getting to and from the airport, and nearby sights from the staff at the front desk · Check-in and check-out go smoothly, and the luggage storage helps anyone with free time before a flight head out to explore · But to be honest, because it's a small hostel, staff numbers are limited · At busy times when lots of people come and go at once you might have to wait at the counter, and the front desk may not be staffed 24 hours like a big hotel · Overall, service is still a strength that makes many guests feel warmly looked after and come back to stay again

What real reviews say (the good and the not-so-good) — pulling from Trip.com, Agoda, Booking.com, and TripAdvisor, the picture is fairly consistent · On the praise side: the location by BTS Phaya Thai and the Airport Rail Link, both an easy walk away, comes up most often, along with clean rooms and bathrooms, comfy beds, large secure lockers that fit a whole bag, free tea/coffee/cookies, friendly staff who help with travel tips, and prices that are great value for a central location · Many international reviews say it's "a ten-dollar-ish hostel that's better than expected" · On the watch-out side: the most-mentioned point is that the building has no elevator and you have to walk up the stairs, which is tough for anyone with a big bag or worn out from a full day out · Next is that the common area and rooms are compact in the hostel way, not spacious; some rooms may catch a bit of noise from inside the building or the soi; and because it's a small place there are no hotel-style amenities like a pool or breakfast · Most of these gripes are things you can manage by setting expectations right from the start, rather than big problems that put people off coming back

"Clean room, comfy bed, lovely staff who helped suggest places to go from day one · The one downside is no elevator, so you have to drag your bag up the stairs — next time I'd pack lighter, but overall it's better value than the price"

Price comparison and value — dorm-bed prices at Cloudy Hostel start at about THB 350–500/night in the normal range, while private rooms like the Double or Twin run around THB 700–1,200/night depending on room type and timing, and may climb during festivals or high season · Compared with other budget hostels and stays in Bangkok, what makes Cloudy Hostel especially good value is the location by both the BTS and the Airport Rail Link, which means you save on taxi fares and travel time every day · Many similarly priced stays in areas far from the trains have to add transport costs and hassle, but here it's just a few minutes' walk to hop on the train · Combine that with clean rooms, large secure lockers, and free tea/coffee, and the overall feeling is that it's great value among budget hostels, especially for anyone planning to ride the trains around Bangkok every day and use the Airport Link to get to and from the airport · If you value easy travel and cleanliness more than a big room or fancy amenities, every baht you spend here feels well returned

What to know before booking — there are a few things that help make the stay smoother · One, the place has no elevator, so if you have a big suitcase or several bags, be ready for the stairs, or ask the hostel which floor your room is on when you book · Two, check-in is from 2:00 PM to 10:00 PM (14:00–22:00) and check-out is before noon, so if your flight lands late or you still have sightseeing after check-out, use the luggage storage on offer · Three, if you're traveling solo and want privacy and security, the female-only dorm and large secure lockers are worth using · Four, it's a small hostel with limited rooms, so book ahead during high season or festivals · Five, because it's a small place, the platforms it's on and the discounts may differ, so compare prices on Agoda, Booking, and Trip.com before deciding, and pick free cancellation if your plans aren't set

The verdict — from all the real reviews, Cloudy Hostel is the best fit for budget travelers who want the easiest location to get around Bangkok, with clean, secure rooms · Its location under a 5-min walk to both BTS Phaya Thai and the Airport Rail Link makes it such good value that a rival at the same price is hard to find, especially for anyone riding the trains every day and using the train to and from the airport · The large secure lockers, free tea/coffee, and friendly staff are details that make the stay warmer · If you're after a luxury stay with a pool, breakfast, or you need an elevator and lots of space, this may not be the answer, and you should look at higher-priced hotels in the same area · But for a budget Bangkok trip where you want the best location for the price, with cleanliness and attentive service — Cloudy Hostel meets that need just about completely, and it's why it keeps earning high review scores in the Phaya Thai area
